DiceStats.Title: Dice statistics

Consent.Question: May your rolls be included in the dice statistics?
Consent.Info: Only how often each face comes up per day is counted – no individual rolls. You see your own statistics, the GM sees everyone’s.
Consent.Change: You can change this at any time in the module settings. If you withdraw consent, nothing is counted any more and your statistics are hidden.

Enabled.Name: Dice statistics
Enabled.Hint: Counts per player and die type how often each face comes up and shows whether the distribution is statistically unusual. Every player is asked for consent first and only sees their own statistics; the GM sees everyone’s. Only counters per day are stored; days older than 12 months are merged.

Consent.Name: Dice statistics: include my rolls
Consent.Hint: Whether your rolls are included in the dice statistics. Without consent nothing is counted; existing data is kept but hidden.

Menu.Label: Open dice statistics
Menu.Hint: Shows how often each face came up and whether that is statistically unusual – players see their own statistics, the GM sees everyone’s.

DiceStats.Disabled: Dice statistics are switched off. The GM can switch them on in the module settings; existing data stays visible.
DiceStats.ChartLabel: Frequency of each face on the d{faces}, expected {expected} each
DiceStats.TestText: Chi-squared goodness-of-fit test: χ² = {chi2} with {df} degrees of freedom, p = {p}. “slightly unusual” from p < {slight}, “clearly unusual” from p < {strong}.
DiceStats.Empty: No rolls yet for this die type and dice.
DiceStats.Note: Digital and physical dice are evaluated separately. With many players and die types, single outliers are pure chance – “unusual” only means a closer look is worthwhile.

Reset.Title: Delete dice statistics
Reset.One: All statistics of {name} will be deleted. This cannot be undone.
Reset.All: All statistics of all players will be deleted. This cannot be undone.

DiceStats.NoConsent: You have not agreed to your rolls being evaluated. You can change this in the module settings.

woundCheck.Title: Wound Assessment
woundCheck.Summary: With a hidden Treat Wounds check, a hero estimates how badly a target is hurt – the more QL, the more precise.
woundCheck.HudButton: Assess the wounds of the targeted token
woundCheck.NoViewer: No character assigned and no token selected.

Page.Intro: How bad is it for the enemy – or for the companion who just went down? A hero with Treat Wounds can tell. How precisely depends on the quality level of the check.
Page.Step1: Target the token (key T or double right-click on the token).
Page.Step2: Right-click your own hero's token and choose the heart button (“Assess the wounds of the targeted token”) on the left of the token menu.
Page.Step3: Roll the Treat Wounds check. It is hidden: only the roller sees the result, the GM only learns that an assessment was made.
Page.Step4: The assessment appears as a whisper in the chat.
Page.QS3: condition and LP range in steps of ten (e.g. 10–20)
Page.QS4: condition and LP range in steps of five (e.g. 15–20)
Page.Conditions: Conditions by remaining LP: unhurt (full LP) · lightly wounded (above 75 %) · clearly wounded (up to 75 %) · badly wounded (up to 50 %) · critically wounded (up to 25 %) · incapacitated (0 LP or less).
Page.Note1: The hero remembers the assessment. Only when the target's LP have changed by at least a quarter of its maximum LP can the hero assess again; until then the button shows the previous assessment.
Page.Note2: With the module “Token Note Hover”, the assessment also appears when hovering over the token – or the note “not examined” or “assessment outdated”.
Page.Note3: Effects placed on the skill itself do not count for this check.
